about.title: San Fernando Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Fernando is a compact, busy city inside Los Angeles County, with families, workers, and small businesses relying on everyday products — from kitchen appliances to power tools to vehicle parts sold along corridors like San Fernando Road and Glenoaks Boulevard. When a product fails because of a flaw in its design, a mistake in manufacturing, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can upend daily life fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. LawProactive is not a law firm; we're a free service that connects San Fernando residents with independent attorneys who evaluate these cases on contingency. If a defective product hurt you, the first step is simple: hold onto the item, and let a qualified attorney look at what happened.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from faulty tools or machinery
Traumatic injuries from failed vehicle components
Poisoning or illness from mislabeled products
Crush or amputation injuries from equipment defects
Fall injuries caused by structurally unsound products

whyChoose.title: Why San Fernando Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. An attorney can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. That means there may be more than one avenue for pursuing accountability.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on physical evidence, keeping the defective item intact and unaltered can be important. An attorney can advise you on how to protect that evidence properly.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally applies strict liability to product defect cases, so the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury, not on proving carelessness. An independent attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me here in San Fernando?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without repairing, discarding, or altering it. This physical evidence is often central to product liability claims. Store it somewhere safe and let an attorney review it as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.

items.question: Can a retailer be responsible, or only the manufacturer?
items.answer: Under California law, liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and retailers who sold the defective product. An attorney can help determine which parties may be involved in your particular case.
